e-4693.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
e-4693.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}]
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_2 := R_2 +(- 4) \cdot R_1$ on $A?$
e-4693.worked_solution:
The operation $R_2:=R_2 + (-4) R_1$ means that we need to add $-4$ times the first row to the second row. 

Carrying out this row operation, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 2 & -1 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4+(-4)(1) & 2+(-4)(2) & -1+(-4)(3) \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -13 \\ 7 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-4694.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
e-4694.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}
$$

 

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ on $A?$
e-4694.worked_solution:
The operation $R_1 \leftrightarrow R_2$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

e-4695.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
e-4695.problem:
Which elementary row operation could transform the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
e-4695.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has been changed is the $2$nd row. 

Now, applying the operation $R_2:=R_2+1 \cdot R_1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4+1\cdot (-4) & 1+1\cdot (-2) & 2+1\cdot 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the transformation could be done by the operation 

$$
R_2:=R_2+1\cdot R_1
$$

or simply

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1.
$$

e-4696.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
e-4696.problem:
Given that
$[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]$ which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
e-4696.worked_solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the matrix X, given by X=[1213−11232].

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R2:=R2−3R1 on X?

a
[1−113−1012−32]
b
[0−7−2121232]
c
[1213−11−1−3−1]
d
[1210−7−2232]
e
[−1−3−11213−11]
Submit

decision.explanation: Replace only row 2: (3,-1,1)-3(1,2,1)=(0,-7,-2). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged, so option d is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}$ on $X?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-3$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3+(-3)(1) & -1+(-3)(2) & 1+(-3)(1) \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the matrix X, given by X=[1213−11232].

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R2:=R2−3R1 on X?

a
[1−113−1012−32]
b
[0−7−2121232]
c
[1213−11−1−3−1]
d
[1210−7−2232]
e
[−1−3−11213−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The operation R2:=R2−3R1 means that we need to add −3 times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

X=[1213−11232]R2:=R2+(−3)⋅R1∼[1213+(−3)(1)−1+(−3)(2)1+(−3)(1)232]∼[1210−7−2232]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}$ on $X?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-3$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3+(-3)(1) & -1+(-3)(2) & 1+(-3)(1) \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 2
before.problem:
Consider the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $B?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $B?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $4$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4+(4)(1) & 12+(4)(3) & 3+(4)(6) \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ -1+1 & 2+3 & 4+6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ 0 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

[136024270−510]
b
[136024271510]
c
[136024250510]
d

e

Submit

EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R2:=R2+4R1 means that we need to add 4 times the first row to the second row.

  • The operation R3:=R3+R1 means that we need to add 1 times the first row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

B=[136−4123−124]R2:=R2+4⋅R1∼[136−4+(4)(1)12+(4)(3)3+(4)(6)−124]∼[13602427−124]R3:=R3+R1∼[13602427−1+12+34+6]∼[136024270510]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms R2 = (0,24,27) and R3 = (0,5,10), with R1 unchanged. This matches option d; option a incorrectly has -5 instead of 5.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $B?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $4$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4+(4)(1) & 12+(4)(3) & 3+(4)(6) \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ -1+1 & 2+3 & 4+6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ 0 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Swap rows 1 and 2, leaving row 3 unchanged. The resulting rows are (3,3,6), (0,8,1), and (4,-1,3), matching option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 & 1 \\ 3 & 3 & 6 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 8 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Replace row 3 with (3,-1,9) + 3(-1,2,4) = (0,5,21). Rows 1 and 2 remain unchanged, giving option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ on $M?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3+(3)(-1) & -1+(3)(2) & 9+(3)(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Consider the matrix M, given by M=[−1248313−19]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R3:=R3+3R1 on M?

a
[−1248310521]
b
[−31−9831−124]
c
[−1248310−19]
d
[3−19831−124]
e
[−1248313−19]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The operation R3:=R3+3R1 means that we need to add 3 times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

M=[−1248313−19]R3:=R3+3⋅R1∼[1−2−48313+(3)(−1)−1+(3)(2)9+(3)(4)]∼[−1248310521]

verification.explanation: R3 becomes (3+3(-1), -1+3(2), 9+3(4)) = (0,5,21), while rows 1 and 2 stay unchanged. This confirms option a and the worked solution's final matrix; its intermediate first row contains a sign typo.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ on $M?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $3$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 9\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 3+(3)(-1) & -1+(3)(2) & 9+(3)(4)\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 4 \\ 8 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 5 & 21\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the matrix A, given by A=[74−115−305−2]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R1↔R2 on A?

a
[15−374−105−2]
b
[05−274−115−3]
c
[74−174−105−2]
d
[74−105−215−3]
e
[47−151−350−2]
Submit

decision.explanation: Swap the first and second rows, leaving the third row unchanged. The resulting rows are (1,5,-3), (7,4,-1), and (0,5,-2), matching option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -3 \\ 7 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the matrix A, given by A=[74−115−305−2]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R1↔R2 on A?

a
[15−374−105−2]
b
[05−274−115−3]
c
[74−174−105−2]
d
[74−105−215−3]
e
[47−151−350−2]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The operation R1↔R2 means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

A=[74−115−305−2]R1↔R2∼[15−374−105−2]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ on $A?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}7 & 4 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & -3 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & -3 \\ 7 & 4 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].

decision.explanation: Subtract row 1 from row 2, including the augmented entry: (1,5,-1,2)-(1,3,2,1)=(0,2,-3,1). The other rows remain unchanged, matching option e.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $X?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & 5+(-1)(3) & -1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(1) \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

Consider the augmented matrix X, given by X=[132115−1234−23]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R1 on X?

a
[132115−1134−23]
b
[132102−3234−23]
c
[132134−2302−31]
d
[1312152−1343−2]
e
[132102−3134−23]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The operation R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R1 means that we need to add −1 times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

X=[132115−1234−23]R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R1∼[13211+(−1)(1)5+(−1)(3)−1+(−1)(2)2+(−1)(1)34−23]∼[132102−3134−23]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that row 2 becomes (1-1,5-3,-1-2,2-1)=(0,2,-3,1). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged, so option e is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ on $X?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & 5+(-1)(3) & -1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(1) \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Replace row 2 with row 2 minus row 3: (5-5,-1-2,2-(-1),1-1)=(0,-3,3,0). Rows 1 and 3 remain unchanged, matching option e.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ on $M?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5+(-1)(5) & -1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(-1) & 1+(-1)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 7
?

Consider the augmented matrix M, given by M=[13915−12152−11]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3 on M?

a
[139152−110−330]
b
[0−33052−111391]
c
[13915−12152−11]
d
[52−115−1211391]
e
[13910−33052−11]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The operation R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3 means that we need to add −1 times the third row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

M=[13915−12152−11]R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3∼[13915+(−1)(5)−1+(−1)(2)2+(−1)(−1)1+(−1)(1)52−11]∼[13910−33052−11]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ on $M?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5+(-1)(5) & -1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(-1) & 1+(-1)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

?

a
[1−18−171−94−21−30]
b
[138−171−946−3−30]

[138−171−94−2−390]

[138−171−94−21−30]

decision.explanation: Multiply every entry of row 3 by -1/3: (6,-3,9,0) becomes (-2,1,-3,0). Rows 1 and 2 remain unchanged, matching option e.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
after.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $-\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:=(-\frac{1}{3})\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 6 & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot (-3) & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 9 & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 8
?

Consider the augmented matrix A, given by A=[138−171−946−390]. What matrix results from carrying out the row operation R3:=−13R3 on A?

a
[1−18−171−94−21−30]
b
[138−171−946−3−30]
c
[13−83−171346−3−30]
d
[138−171−94−2−390]
e
[138−171−94−21−30]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The operation R3:=−13R3 means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by −13.

Multiplying the 3rd row by −13, we obtain the following:

A=[138−171−946−390]R3:=(−13)⋅R3∼[138−171−94(−13)⋅6(−13)⋅(−3)(−13)⋅9(−13)⋅0]∼[138−171−94−21−30]

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that multiplying row 3 by -1/3 gives (-2,1,-3,0). Rows 1 and 2 remain unchanged, so option e is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
content.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $-\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:=(-\frac{1}{3})\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 6 & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot (-3) & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 9 & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 9
before.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $U,$ given by

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $U?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Consider the augmented matrix U, given by U=[102−202060−1−34]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on U?

R2:=12R2R3:=R3+R2

a
[102−2010600−310]
b
[102−2020601−310]
c
[102−2020602−310]

[102−2010300−37]
e

Submit

decision.explanation: First halve row 2 to get (0,1,0,3). Then add this updated row to row 3: (0,-1,-3,4)+(0,1,0,3)=(0,0,-3,7). Row 1 stays unchanged, giving option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $U,$ given by

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $U?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}$ means that we need to multiply the second row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{2}.$

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0+0 & -1+1 & -3+0 & 4+3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

Consider the augmented matrix U, given by U=[102−202060−1−34]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on U?

R2:=12R2R3:=R3+R2

a
[102−2010600−310]
b
[102−2020601−310]
c
[102−2020602−310]
d
[102−2010300−37]
e
[10−220103013−7]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R2:=12R2 means that we need to multiply the second row of the matrix by 12.

  • The operation R3:=R3+R2 means that we need to add 1 times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

U=[102−202060−1−34]R2:=12⋅R2∼[102−201030−1−34]R3:=R3+R2∼[102−201030+0−1+1−3+04+3]∼[102−2010300−37]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $U,$ given by

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $U?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}$ means that we need to multiply the second row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{2}.$

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0+0 & -1+1 & -3+0 & 4+3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 10
before.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the augmented matrix V, given by V=[−19−2644679057]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on V?

R1↔R3R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3

a
[90574467−19−26]
b
[4467−109−7−19057]
c
[90575−581−19−26]
d
[9057−5410−19−26]
e
[−19−26−54109057]
Submit

decision.explanation: First swap rows 1 and 3. Then subtract the updated row 3 from row 2: (4,4,6,7)-(-1,9,-2,6)=(5,-5,8,1). This gives option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 10
?

Consider the augmented matrix V, given by V=[−19−2644679057]. What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on V?

R1↔R3R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3

a
[90574467−19−26]
b
[4467−109−7−19057]
c
[90575−581−19−26]
d
[9057−5410−19−26]
e
[−19−26−54109057]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Let's list the required operations:

  • The operation R1↔R3 means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

  • The operation R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3 means that we need to add −1 times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

V=[−19−2644679057]R1↔R3∼[90574467−19−26]R2:=R2+(−1)⋅R3∼[90574+(−1)(−1)4+(−1)(9)6+(−1)(−2)7+(−1)(6)−19−26]∼[90575−581−19−26]

content.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix
content.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

before.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $E$ into the matrix $F$, where

$$

Question 11
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix E into the matrix F, where E=[5−238−37−31−3],F=[5−23−31−38−37]?

a
R2:=(−38)⋅R2
b
R2:=R2+(−5)⋅R1
c
R3:=R3−R1
d
R2↔R3
e
R3:=(−83)⋅R3
Submit

decision.explanation: The first row stays unchanged, while the second and third rows exchange positions. Thus the required operation is R2 ↔ R3, option d.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $E$ into the matrix $F$, where

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7 \\ -3 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,F=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & 1 & -3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st row is the same in both matrices. The only rows that have changed are the $2$nd row and the $3$rd row.   

By considering the given row operations that change both the $2$nd and the $3$rd row, we notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}E & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7 \\ -3 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & 1 & -3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =F.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $K$ into the matrix $L$, where

$$
K=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}K & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =L.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}.
$$

First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}K & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =L.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}.
$$

before.html:
Question 13
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix C into the matrix D, where C=[−21−1772−616],D=[−63−3772−616]?

a
R1:=R1+(−47)⋅R2
b
R1:=13⋅R1
c
R1:=R1+R2
d
R1↔R3
e
R1:=3⋅R1
Submit

decision.explanation: Multiplying row 1 by 3 gives 3(-2,1,-1)=(-6,3,-3), while rows 2 and 3 remain unchanged. Therefore option e transforms C into D.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix  $C$ into the matrix $D$, where 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -3 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -3 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =D.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=3\cdot {R}_{1}.
$$

C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -3 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & -1 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=3\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-6 & 3 & -3 \\ 7 & 7 & 2 \\ -6 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =D.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:=3\cdot {R}_{1}.
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 10 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $2$nd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $3$rd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $3$rd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 10 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}\cdot {R}_{3}.
$$

Question 14
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix A into the matrix B, where A=[52−3−802105−5],B=[52−3−80221−1]?

a
R2:=R2+R3
b
R3:=R3+R2
c
R3:=R3+(−2)⋅R1
d
R2:=R2+(−310)⋅R3
e
R3:=15⋅R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the 1st and the 2nd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the 3rd row.

By considering the given row operations that modify the 3rd row, we notice that

A=[52−3−802105−5]R3:=15⋅R3∼[52−3−80221−1]=B.

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=15⋅R3.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
content.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 10 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $2$nd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $3$rd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $3$rd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 10 & 5 & -5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -3 \\ -8 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{5}\cdot {R}_{3}.
$$

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix X into the matrix W, where X=[00556101−1−3],W=[5−5−1056101−1−3]?

a
R1↔R2
b
R1:=R1+5R3
c
R3:=R3+5R1
d
R1:=R1+R2
e
R1:=R1+15R3
Submit

decision.explanation: Adding five times row 3 to row 1 gives (0,0,5)+5(1,-1,-3)=(5,-5,-10). Rows 2 and 3 remain unchanged, so option b is correct.

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $X$ into the matrix $W$, where

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{3}.
$$

after.html:
Question 15
?

Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix X into the matrix W, where X=[00556101−1−3],W=[5−5−1056101−1−3]?

a
R1↔R2
b
R1:=R1+5R3
c
R3:=R3+5R1
d
R1:=R1+R2
e
R1:=R1+15R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that the 2nd and the 3rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the 1st row.

By considering the given row operations that modify the 1st row, we notice that

X=[00556101−1−3]R1:=R1+5⋅R3∼[5−5−1056101−1−3]=W.

Therefore, the required row operation is

R1:=R1+5R3.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
content.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $X$ into the matrix $W$, where

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $1$st row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =W.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{3}.
$$

Question 16
?

Given A=[148181601224], which of the following elementary row operations makes a22=0?

a
R2↔R3
b
R2:=R2+(−1)R1
c
R2↔R1
d
R2:=R2+(−2)R3
e
R2:=R2+(−2)R1
Submit

decision.explanation: The entry a22 becomes 8+(-2)(4)=0 when twice row 1 is subtracted from row 2. Therefore option e is correct.

after.name: Question 16
after.problem:
Given 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 8 & 16 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{22}=0?$
after.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 8 & 16 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 8 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}.

Question 16
?

Given A=[148181601224], which of the following elementary row operations makes a22=0?

a
R2↔R3
b
R2:=R2+(−1)R1
c
R2↔R1
d
R2:=R2+(−2)R3
e
R2:=R2+(−2)R1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R2:=R2+(−2)R1.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

A=[148181601224]R2:=R2+(−2)⋅R1∼[148−10001224]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R2:=R2+(−2)R1.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e: subtracting twice row 1 from row 2 gives (1,8,16)-2(1,4,8)=(-1,0,0), so a22 becomes 0.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 8 & 16 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{22}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 8 & 16 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 8 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 12 & 24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1}.
$$

Question 17
?

Given that C=[462364231], which of the following elementary row operations makes a22=0?

a
R2:=R2+(−2)R3
b
R2↔R3
c
R1↔R3
d
R2:=R2+(−3)R1
e
R2:=(−2)R2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R2:=R2+(−2)R3.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

C=[462364231]R2:=R2+(−2)⋅R3∼[462−102231]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R2:=R2+(−2)R3.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given that
$C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{22}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 2 \\ 3 & 6 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3}.
$$

Question 18
?

Given M=[130921764], which of the following elementary row operations makes a32=0?

a
R3:=R3+(−3)R2
b
R3:=R3+2R1
c
R1↔R2
d
R3↔R2
e
R3:=(−3)R3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R3:=R3+(−3)R2.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

M=[130921764]R3:=R3+(−3)⋅R2∼[130921−2001]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R3:=R3+(−3)R2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms that R3 becomes (7,6,4)-3(9,2,1)=(-20,0,1), making a32=0. Thus option a is correct.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given 
$M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 9 & 2 & 1 \\ 7 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{32}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 9 & 2 & 1 \\ 7 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 9 & 2 & 1 \\ -20 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2}.
$$

Question 19
?

Given that X=[−8106083903], which of the following elementary row operations makes a13=0?

a
R1:=R1+2R3
b
R1:=R1+(−2)R2
c
R1↔R2
d
R1:=(−2)R1
e
R1↔R3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R1:=R1+(−2)R2.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

X=[−8106083903]R1:=R1+(−2)⋅R2∼[−8−60083903]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R1:=R1+(−2)R2.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given that
$X=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 10 & 6 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$,
which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{13}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 10 & 6 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2)\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-8 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 & 3 \\ 9 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2}.
$$

Question 20
?

Given T=[6482122−6−4], which of the following elementary row operations makes a23=0?

a
R2↔R1
b
R2:=12R2
c
R2↔R3
d
R2:=R2+12R3
e
R2:=R2+14R1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

R2:=R2+12R3.

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

T=[6482122−6−4]R2:=R2+12⋅R3∼[6483−20212]

Therefore, the required row operation is

R2:=R2+12R3.

content.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform a Given Entry to a Desired Value
content.problem:
Given 
$T=[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 8 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}]$,
 which of the following elementary row operations makes ${a}_{23}=0?$
content.worked_solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation 

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 8 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -6 & -4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & 4 & 8 \\ 3 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{3}.
$$
